chunks: And ʿAbdullāh ibn Sinān narrated from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

If the mule driver does not remain settled in his home except for five days or less, he shortens in his travel by day and completes the night prayer, and the fast of the month of Ramadan is upon him. But if he has a stay in the town to which he goes for ten days or more, and he returns to his home and has a stay of ten days or more, he shortens in his travel and breaks the fast.

key_terms.أَفْطَرَ: broke the fast, meaning he did not fast due to the travel ruling
key_terms.الْمُكَارِي: a mule driver or transport worker who travels regularly for livelihood
key_terms.صَلَاةَ اللَّيْلِ: the night prayer, here meaning the prayer performed at night in full
key_terms.صَوْمُ شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ: the fasting of the month of Ramadan
key_terms.مُقَامٌ: a period of stay or residence in a place

ai.seo_question: What are the travel prayer and fasting rulings for a mukārī who frequently travels?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the legal ruling for a mukārī, a transport worker whose occupation involves frequent travel, regarding salat and sawm in travel. It distinguishes between one who does not settle for long at home and one who stays ten days or more at destinations and at home, affecting whether he shortens prayer and whether he fasts or breaks the fast in Ramadan.
